questions.q: What does being in the box mean?
a: Seeing others as objects rather than people with needs
Hiding your true feelings from your coworkers
Working alone without support from a team
Following orders without asking any questions
questions.why: Lesson 1 says self-deception makes you value your comfort above others.

questions.q: What does the summary say self-deception does to your view of others?
a: You see them as you assume they are, not as they really are
You see them more clearly than you did before
You treat every person exactly equally
You become overly trusting of total strangers
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the false belief that your needs matter more distorts your view.

questions.q: How does self-deception affect an argument with a spouse, according to the summary?
a: You justify your own wishes and call theirs unrealistic
You avoid the topic until it disappears
You agree to whatever they want to keep peace
You ask a friend to decide the matter for you
questions.why: Lesson 2 says you inflate your virtues and exaggerate their flaws.

questions.q: What is the way out of self-deception?
a: Act on your instinct to help people in need
Avoid the people who annoy you most
Win more arguments at work and at home
Learn to hide your emotions more effectively
questions.why: Lesson 3 says changing your mindset, not just behavior, beats the box.

questions.q: What benefit does the summary promise for getting out of the box?
a: People focus on the work instead of blaming each other
You gain a promotion and a higher salary
Your family stops disagreeing with you
You no longer need to apologize to anyone
questions.why: Lesson 3 says relationships ease and leaders create a culture of responsibility.
